title: Smart Watch based Integration System for Habituating Face Paralysis Monitoring
summary: VIT describes a facial-paralysis monitoring workflow, while dataset collection and exercise-recognition model development remain planned.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The submission labels the system active but also identifies core dataset collection and model development as future work. Its intended benefits are earlier monitoring, appropriate intervention, and support for facial exercises. It gives no measured patient improvement or timely-treatment event.
purpose: Support facial-paralysis monitoring and rehabilitation exercises.
system: Smart Watch based Integration System for Habituating Face Paralysis Monitoring

ratings.reason: Facial-paralysis monitoring is labeled active, but model building and dataset collection remain future work and no patient outcome is given.

ai_role.statement: The account does not isolate AI’s contribution from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025). Project-submitted account, current as of June 2025. ITU provides no independent outcome evaluation.
evidence.title: Use Case 25: Smart Watch based Integration System for Habituating Face Paralysis Monitoring

produced_by: The account does not establish conditions sufficient to reproduce the benefit.
must_hold: The account does not establish requirements for reproducing the benefit in other settings.

headline: A smartwatch workflow aims to monitor facial paralysis
claim_basis: Sources: the makers' report. The cited evidence includes no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
